name: FASER
summary: FASER is located in CERN LHC tunnel TI12, 480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point. It is a dedicated far-forward new-particle experiment that also measures collider neutrinos.
detection_principle: Light long-lived particles are sought far forward along the collision axis after traversing rock and machine shielding and decaying inside the detector, using energetic tracks and electromagnetic energy.

results.summary: An enlarged accepted decay region and track-topology coverage set new dark-photon limits, without discovery.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
